For the winning-target sets write X=(a, b, b), Y=(a, b, b-1), and f=f(b, b-1), with b<=a<d(b). Middle-cut target lists coincide. Bottom-cut lists differ only by the extra target Y of X. Top cuts below b coincide in both positions, so their outcomes need not be evaluated. The remaining top cuts of X cannot be P because their top is below d(b); those of Y can be P only at top f. When f>a, none of these differing top cuts is P and Y itself is N, proving W(X)=W(Y). When f=a, Y is an extra P target of X. When f<a, (f, b, b-1) is a P target of Y but is not any one-move target of X. The bound a<=b+124<f<d(b) gives exactly the equal-set case. No unbounded-lag or proof-grammar exhaustion claim follows.
